displayName: inflect assistant is REFUSING most attempts — users blocked from a working feature (#3856)

conditions.displayName: assistant refusal rate at or above 33% over the last hour
assistant refusal reporting stopped — absence is not health

documentation.content:
The in-product assistant REFUSED a third or more of its attempts over the last
hour. Users are being blocked from a feature that works.

WHY THIS IS PAGED RATHER THAN CHARTED. A refused user usually does not report
it -- they stop asking. So the failure mode is silent by construction: the
process is healthy, `/api/readyz` is green, and the only symptom is an absence
of use that looks like low adoption. A guard misfiring on ordinary compliance
prose would look exactly like that.

HOW THE RATE IS COMPUTED, because the denominator is not the obvious one.
`runGoverned` asserts on the guard verdict BEFORE producing an answer and
THROWS on review-required, so a refused turn writes no `AiDecisionLog` row at
all. Dividing refusals by decision-log rows would therefore divide by the turns
that were NOT refused, and would read LOWER the worse things got. Attempts are
the sum: rows that got through, plus guard events that stopped one.

    assistant_refusal_pct = assistant_refusals / (assistant_turns + assistant_refusals)

Both components are published beside the rate, because a percentage with no
denominator cannot be read at 03:00 -- 100% of two attempts and 100% of two
hundred are different incidents.

WHAT TO DO. The reporter writes the breakdown by guard source to its journal
whenever it crosses the threshold:

    journalctl -u assistant-health-reporter.service -n 50

| source | means |
|---|---|
| assistant | the user's own question tripped the injection scanner. A spike here is usually one tenant pasting document text into the prompt box. |
| assistant:page-context | the PAGE CONTEXT tripped it -- route, filters or selected ids. This is the surface added in #3841 and the one to suspect after a filter or URL change, because its content is not typed by the user. |
| assistant:outbound | the ANSWER tripped the egress guard. A spike here is the model, not the input. |

A SPIKE CONFINED TO ONE SOURCE IS THE USEFUL CASE. All three rising together is
a guard-rule or guard-mode change; one rising alone names its own cause.

NOT COVERED, so the absence of this alert is not an all-clear: the
guidance-route refusal (#3845) writes a log line rather than a row and is not
counted; nor is the 429 stream-capacity refusal, which is a load signal and
would mislead if folded in here. A tenant in AUDIT guard mode refuses nothing
and contributes nothing, correctly.
